name_note: GTDB g__Limivicinus corresponds to Candidatus Limivicinus; its species are uncultured placeholders, and the retrieved literature describes it in animal gut and rumen communities rather than in humans.

sentences.text: In that study, members of Candidatus Limivicinus transcribed the isethionate-producing sulfo-transketolase pathway.
A study of gastrointestinal nitrogen metabolism reported that a soybean meal diet selectively enriched protein degraders including Limivicinus in the rumen.
A strain-resolved comparison of cattle rumen microbiomes reported enrichment of the Limivicinus genus in Angus rumen.
In faecal metagenomes from wild and domestic equids, genomes co-carrying antibiotic resistance genes were predominantly assigned to anaerobic gut genera including Limivicinus.
